title: Lightweight Fault Isolation: Practical, Efficient, and Secure Software Sandboxing
problem: Software-based fault isolation systems must efficiently isolate untrusted code while balancing performance, trusted code base size, and scalability, particularly for ARM64 systems used in cloud and serverless computing.
motivation: Cloud and serverless computing require systems to run untrusted code with low latency and minimal context switch overhead.
method: LFI runs tens of thousands of isolated environments (4GiB sandboxes) within a single address space by rewriting compiled machine code directly (binary instrumentation), without needing a compiler. It ensures all memory reads and writes (loads and stores) and program jumps stay within sandbox boundaries by checking the code once before it runs (static verification), using a small verification program to minimize the amount of code you have to trust. The system also includes defenses against Spectre attacks and supports programming language features like exception handling and SIMD (single instruction, multiple data — a hardware feature for processing many values at once).
key_novelty: LFI is the first practical system that isolates tens of thousands of sandboxes on ARM64 processors (used in cloud computing) with just 7% performance overhead and a minimal amount of code you have to trust.
contributions: Multi-sandbox SFI design for ARM64 with 7% SPEC 2017 runtime overhead
Compiler-independent implementation with small static verifier for TCB minimization
Spectre attack hardening for software-based isolation
Broad software support for exceptions, SIMD, and multiple languages

metrics.other: 7% runtime overhead on SPEC 2017; supports tens of thousands of 4GiB sandboxes
